conclusion_scope: Bounded classification for WP-DW-05 only. No entry upgrades an untested capability into a public contract.

limitations.rationale: CITY completeness is domain/source-universe owned. DW-02 accepted complete declared production-query universes without changing the generic seam. DW-05 does not generalize this to all CITY semantics.
PA losslessness is schema/source-oracle owned and was accepted for PA-01..05. The neutral probe neither re-proves nor broadens it.
DW-04 is valid only for its frozen task/model/configuration universe. DW-05 preserves that bound rather than converting it into a general adoption claim.
Comparison to effective Unity state requires accepted H1 observation/projection evidence and is not exercised by the in-repo neutral DW probe.
In-repository project references do not prove package/version distribution or consumption from a fresh repository.
DW exposes accepted content-shape facts but has no accepted effort/cost authority. A future reviewed planning model owns that step.
Runtime/Unity conformance is not a Design World source-projection guarantee.
Design-implied content shape does not establish actual source-catalogue coverage.
Future accepted PA material may require PA projection/schema extension. That is not evidence that the current generic fact/relation/provenance seam failed.
DW-04 was a bounded fail-closed conformance trial, not a population estimate. DW-GATE must preserve that interpretation.
CITY, PA and one neutral synthetic graph are three bounded shapes. They are insufficient evidence for arbitrary-domain universality.
Generating production briefs from queries is a downstream product/tooling decision, not an exercised DW-05 capability.
Replay-backed QA needs a separately accepted replay/evidence boundary.
Narrative knowledge validation requires a separately reviewed knowledge model and oracle.

CITY and PA provider implementations are co-located with the generic Arkus.DesignWorld assembly. The neutral probe consumes only generic public types and the generic implementation has no dependency on CITY/PA symbols, so this does not falsify the in-repo seam. It is relevant to later packaging/public-boundary design.

Arkus.DesignWorld.csproj still carries a comment and WarningsNotAsErrors suppression described as temporary during DW-03. It is not required by the neutral probe and is not repaired inside DW-05 merely to improve optics.

Removing a domain-required relation while preserving a structurally valid graph remains GREEN under the generic structural validator and RED under the independent neutral consumer oracle. This is consistent with the accepted invariant boundary: H0/DW represents relations; the consumer owns semantic necessity/cardinality.
